hypothesis_text: Our single-item auction mechanism is incentive-compatible for LLM bidders: across 50 trials with random private valuations drawn from U[0,1], bidders bid within 5% of their valuation on average, demonstrating truthful revelation.
flaw_description: Incentive compatibility is a property of the mechanism (dominant-strategy IC, Bayesian-Nash IC), proven analytically by reference to payoff structure — not a property established by observing that bidders bid near their values. A first-price auction would also produce bids near valuations under risk aversion, yet first-price is NOT incentive-compatible. The empirical observation does not establish the formal property.
expected_critique_targets: incentive compatibility is an analytical property, not empirical
near-truthful bids are consistent with non-IC mechanisms
needs proof for the payoff structure, not observation
context: Week-4 single-item auction rung sketch; conflates empirical bid behavior with mechanism property.
